prompt: Create an atmospheric watercolor illustration for the OVERVIEW of an educational course about earth sciences and field exploration. Match a soft field-atlas style: delicate watercolor washes on warm ivory cream paper with very subtle grain, fine pencil/pen contours, muted ochre, sandy beige, soft amber, distant grey-blue mountains, pale drifting clouds. Wide landscape composition, 16:9. Show ONLY the Earth's visible surface: broad rolling steppe/meadow in the foreground, mountain silhouettes and open sky, and a very small distant drilling derrick and a small pumpjack as contextual silhouettes on the horizon, viewed from far away. Quiet spacious elegant illustration, equipment subordinate to the landscape. Everything underground is completely invisible. STRICTLY NO cross-section, cutaway, subsurface diagram, strata/layers shown in a slice, borehole, exposed underground, fossils, ammonites, core samples, thin sections, graphs, curves, labels, captions, text, letters, numbers, readable screens, logos or watermark. This is an ambient landscape, not a scientific diagram and not a claim about any chapter. Use the entire frame for the artwork with soft edges and airy paper-colored areas; no frame or inset.
usage: General atmospheric surface landscape for the course overview. Not chapter evidence.
